<objective>
Fix three engine-side bounds that state one property and deliver a weaker one.

- **MD-01** — `SOURCE_ROWS_PER_MAP_MAX` is derived and documented as a ROW bound and enforced as a
  declared-SOURCES bound, so the real ceiling is twice the stated one. This is load-bearing: HI-04's
  fixed convergence inequality carries a `2 *` factor that exists precisely because of the mismatch.
- **LO-01** — `decodeInlineMap` materialises the whole payload string before the size gate, and
  `findAnnouncement` has already sliced to end-of-line before that, so an 8 MiB single-line body costs
  two full-length copies on the QuickJS thread before the "cheap comparison" refuses it.
- **LO-02** — `announce.ts` treats only `\n` as a line terminator, so a `data:` URL absorbs the rest of
  a `\r`-, `U+2028`- or `U+2029`-delimited file. Contained today (`isCanonicalBase64` rejects it) but
  it is what makes LO-01's slice unbounded.

**The sequencing is the point of this plan, not an implementation detail.** `ROWS_INSERTED_PER_ITERATION_MAX`
is `ROWS_INSERTED_PER_ARTIFACT_MAX + 2 * SOURCE_ROWS_PER_MAP_MAX`, and that constant's own docblock
records why: the gate's unit does not match its derivation, so an insert bound using the stated number
would be half of what the code can actually do. Fixing MD-01 makes the factor 1. Change the factor
FIRST and the inequality understates the insert side for the length of one commit. Fix the gate first
and the inequality only gets slacker — which the docblock also says, and which this plan holds it to.

Output: three bounds that mean what they say, and an inequality that is true at every commit.
</objective>

Make the two cheap refusals actually cheap.

**`parse.ts`.** In the prefix loop, compare `url.length - prefix.length` against
`encodedCeiling(maxBytes)` and return the `too_large` refusal BEFORE `url.slice`. The length is
knowable without a copy. Keep the existing post-slice checks — empty, canonical-base64 — exactly where
they are; only the size gate moves ahead of the allocation.

Correct the docblock at the same time. It currently claims the gate fires before ANYTHING is
allocated, which is now true of the string as well as of the decoded buffer. Say which allocation each
half of the sentence refers to, so a later reader does not have to re-derive the distinction LO-01
found.

**`announce.ts`.** Bound the URL slice. The longest legal announcement URL is
`ANNOUNCEMENT_PREFIX_MAX + encodedCeiling(MAP_MAX_BYTES)` by the derivation `SOURCEMAP_TAIL_WINDOW_BYTES`
already states; slice at the smaller of that bound and the terminator offset. A URL longer than the
bound cannot be a map this build will accept, so cutting it costs nothing that was reachable and saves
a full-body copy on a body with no terminator.

Take the bound from `thresholds.ts` rather than restating the arithmetic — `SOURCEMAP_TAIL_WINDOW_BYTES`
is already `ceil(MAP_MAX_BYTES * 4/3) + ANNOUNCEMENT_PREFIX_MAX`, so the value exists and importing it
keeps one derivation rather than two.

**Cases.** `parse.spec.ts`: an oversized payload refused `too_large`, asserted through the public
result rather than by instrumenting allocation, plus a boundary case one byte under. `announce.spec.ts`:
a body with no terminator after the marker, asserting the returned URL length is at or below the bound.
Both must be RED against the shipped implementation in the over-bound direction — record what the
pre-fix code returned.
  </action>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| target response body → engine parse path | Every byte `findAnnouncement` and `decodeInlineMap` see is chosen by the target, and both run synchronously on the QuickJS thread that also serves live browsing. |
| declared map structure → plugin database | A map's `sources` array length decides how many rows one consumer iteration writes. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-07-58 | Denial of Service | `decodeInlineMap` and `findAnnouncement` string materialisation | medium | mitigate | The size refusal moves ahead of the slice in `decodeInlineMap`, and the announcement URL is bounded at `ANNOUNCEMENT_PREFIX_MAX + encodedCeiling(MAP_MAX_BYTES)` rather than at end-of-file. An 8 MiB single-line body with an oversized inline map then costs offset arithmetic instead of two full-length copies on the proxy thread. |
| T-07-59 | Tampering | `findAnnouncement`'s line-terminator scan | low | mitigate | Four bounded `indexOf` calls, smallest offset wins, no pattern. A body delimited by lone CR, LS or PS can no longer let the `data:` URL absorb following code. Contained before this change — `isCanonicalBase64` refused the result — so the fix removes an unbounded slice rather than an unsound parse. |
| T-07-60 | Denial of Service | `absorb`'s aggregate gate against `SOURCE_ROWS_PER_MAP_MAX` | medium | mitigate | A legal map declaring 2,048 distinct one-line sources, well under `MAP_MAX_BYTES`, currently passes and inserts up to 4,096 rows in one consumer iteration against a 512-row sweep cap. Enforcing in rows halves the reachable ceiling to the documented one, and the retention convergence inequality is asserted true at both commits that change it. |

No package-manager install task exists in this plan, so no supply-chain threat row applies.
</threat_model>
